name: Jeroboam II (son of Joash)
title: The Mighty Restorer of Israel
summary: Jeroboam II was king over the Northern Kingdom of Israel for 41 years and one of the most powerful kings in its history. During his reign, Israel experienced great territorial expansion and economic prosperity, but he continued in the sins of Jeroboam I with idol worship. The prophets Amos and Hosea ministered during his time and warned against Israel's moral decay.

keyEvents.title: Becomes King of Israel
keyEvents.description: Jeroboam II became king over Israel in Samaria and reigned for 41 years, the longest reign of any king in the Northern Kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Restored Israel's Borders
keyEvents.description: He restored Israel's borders from Lebo-Hamat to the Sea of the Arabah, in accordance with the prophecy of Jonah.

keyEvents.title: Continued in Jeroboam's Sins
keyEvents.description: Despite military success, Jeroboam II did what was evil in the Lord's sight and continued the idolatry that Jeroboam I had introduced.

keyEvents.title: The warnings of the prophet Amos
keyEvents.description: During the reign of Jeroboam II, Amos prophesied against Israel's social injustice and religious hypocrisy, predicting judgment upon the nation.

keyEvents.title: The ministry of the prophet Hosea
keyEvents.description: Hosea began his prophetic service under Jeroboam II and proclaimed God's love to unfaithful Israel.

keyEvents.title: The death of Jeroboam II
keyEvents.description: Jeroboam II died and rested with his fathers, and his son Zechariah became king in his place, but was killed after only six months.
